annotation.method: Codex read the complete 47-page local PDF sequentially and, during the audit-driven P19-T2 and P19-T3 rebuilds, rechecked Algorithms 1-2, equations (3.2)-(3.20), Theorems 3.1, 3.3, and 3.4, and Appendices A, C, and D in extracted text and rendered source pages; searched the frozen library and compiled private N/L constructions for the rebuilt targets.

rejected_candidates.reason: These establish the computational model and hypotheses rather than a concise selected conclusion. Their four error sources are retained in T2's exact modular aggregation.

rejected_candidates.candidate: the complete specialized statement of Theorem 3.2
rejected_candidates.reason: P19-T2 selects the general modular Theorem 3.1, while P19-T3 selects the specialized right and flexible results in Theorems 3.3-3.4. The left-preconditioned theorem would duplicate that framework without contributing to the selected right-versus-flexible implementation distinction.
The rho_M and rho_b quantities make a compact exact comparison less clean. The right/flexible pair shares common terms and exposes the paper's critical implementation distinction directly.
This is a property of the synthetic matrix generator used to structure experiments, not the paper's main rounding-error contribution.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Tables 2-3 and the six strategy recommendations in Sections 4.2-4.3
rejected_candidates.reason: Several recommendations combine simplified asymptotic bounds with problem-dependent or explicitly qualified empirical behavior. T3 captures the exact theoretical right/flexible comparison that drives one of the strongest recommendations.
These report finite experiments and iteration counts rather than universally quantified mathematical results.
These are practical experiments whose outliers are explicitly noted as not always explained by the simplified theory.

rejected_candidates.candidate: backward-error, implementation-performance, and industrial-software directions in Section 6
rejected_candidates.reason: The paper identifies these as open issues or future work, not completed results.

T1.decision: Use the exact upper perturbation-norm inequality in equation (C.8), which is a direct specialization of the frozen Euclidean triangle theorem.

T2.decision: Use Theorem 3.1, including Algorithm 2's modular hypotheses, a dimension derived by the cited first-loss MGS argument rather than supplied as execution data, and the complete normalized first-order forward-error bound (3.8) derived from raw Appendix-A gains. Preserve the paper's unspecified c(n,k) value and qualitative second-order notation without inventing polynomial coefficients or a precision filter.

T3.decision: Use the complete conditional existential attainable-forward-error results of Theorems 3.3 and 3.4 as separately quantified claims, derive both dimensions through the first-loss MGS argument, require the full source conditions at every terminal-or-near-dependence candidate as in Appendix C, retain all five terms of condition (3.16), and preserve Remark 4's exact identification of the right-only preconditioner-reapplication term. Use static qualitative first-order semantics, source-authorized square condition-number choices, raw Appendix-C/D gains, and no preselected key dimensions or precision filter.

selection_policy: Represent the source's unspecified low-degree c(n,k) by its value at the selected dimensions, and parameterize the qualitative second-order semantics instead of inventing polynomial coefficients or an asymptotic variable.
When Section 2 writes an unqualified square condition number, expose the source-authorized Frobenius or induced-2 choice explicitly and apply it consistently to the matrix and its certified inverse.
Represent the paper's four modular error sources and right/flexible precision distinction explicitly.
Do not promote empirical heatmaps, iteration counts, qualified recommendations, or future-work claims to theorem targets.
Keep every public definition free of NumStability imports.
Assign tiers only from the 24 modules in metadata/library_olean.json.
